chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Caruso's Sunday afternoons at Mrs. Eggleston's
summary: Whaley recalls the five-piece band, the club's colored entertainment, and Caruso directing operas for $200 on Sundays.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Eddie Cantor come down there, he sang "Margie," Row, Row, Row" and he used to sing a whole lot of numbers and I used to catch them and I told you about Enrico Caruso.
No, I got to hear, the great tenor singer.
The great tenor singer. He used to come down there on a Sunday afternoon and I told you about this.
Well, let me hear it.
He wouldn't sing, he'd tell the people you got $2,000 I sing, but --
What was this a restaurant he came to.
No, it was a club like. You have a big dancehall and a big dining room and the people would dine and then they'd come in the dancehall.
Was it an Italian place.
NO, it was Mrs. Eggleston.
Oh, yeah, you mentioned her name.
She run the place. It's one of the best spots on the north shore for entertainment, see, they had all colored entertainment there, the best. I had Carl White.
What did Carl White do.
He played piano, I mean played guitar and sang. Clarence Cummings, he played the violin. Leroy Tibbs played tenor and Willie -- gee, I forgot his name.
What did he play.
Willie played the drums. We had quite a good team there, they were very goöd. We used to -- if we didn't make $10 a night, we weren't doing anything.
Apiece.
Yeah, $10 apiece.
So Caruso came in...
And he would direct operas, we'd have

all the operas, don't play no dance music on Sundays out there, play all operas and overtures and everything and he used to direct them, tell us what to play and everything. We'd drink champagne and afterwards he'd give us $200 for the afternoon show.
Enrico Caruso, the great tenor.
That's it.
Do you remember any of the songs he used to play on Sundays.
Oh, we used to play 'Merry Wives of Windsor', the operas, 'Poet and Peasant.'
(Humming)
What's the name of the otherone, like the Windmill. I can't never think of that name.
That's all right.
(Humming) and --
How many pieces did you have in your band.
Only had five.
You would play everything.
Sure, we played the whole thing. We played everything. Play overtures and --
Was Caruso livjng in Boston then.
You know, when he come to Boston Opera House he'd live in a hotel and then he'd come down Sundays. He'd come down Sundays to enjoy himself, one Sunday I went
hunting and I didn't catch a thing, and when he left -- when I come there he had left a note, don't go hunting on my day. All the big shots come down there. Babe Ruth, he used to come in there.
